subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Dead Load vs. Live Load
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dead Load vs. Live Load.

hook.text: The Golden Gate Bridge weighs 887,000 tons. That weight never changes. But the real danger is what moves.

buildup.text: Dead load is the bridge's own weight — steel, concrete, cables. It's constant and predictable.

discovery.text: Live load is everything that changes — traffic, pedestrians, wind, rain, even temperature expansion.

twist.text: A marching army once collapsed a bridge. Synchronized footsteps created a resonance the structure couldn't handle.

climax.text: Engineers now design for worst-case scenarios: maximum traffic, hurricane winds, and earthquakes combined.

punchline.text: The bridge's weight is safe. It's yours that's dangerous.

quiz.question: What is the difference between dead load and live load on a bridge?
options: Dead load is damage; live load is the original construction weight
Dead load is the bridge's own weight; live load is variable forces
Dead load is underground; live load is above the surface
